- **second tooling discovery this sub-step (new)**: MCP tool schema introspection (`tools/list`) shows `func_query`'s `queries` param is an array of **filter objects** (`filter`/`name_regex`/`min_size`/`max_size`/`has_type`/`offset`/`count`/`sort_by`/`descending`), not plain strings — passing plain strings (as in the ARGUMENTS example `{"queries":["codexmate_lib::commands::"]}`) is silently accepted but the filter is not applied, silently returning the first 10 functions in default order unfiltered (confirmed: identical byte-for-byte 10-item output for two different plain-string queries). ### Sub-entry — mac-shard-3/8 BLOCKED: IDA mac 1.1.8 IDB is decompiling the x86_64 slice, not arm64 (2026-07-11)

- **owner-gate re-check before write**: `grep -c 'mac-shard-3'` on INDEX.jsonl at time of this sub-step = 0; `intermediate/aimami/1.1.8/macos-arm64/version-delta/buckets/mac-shard-3.json` does not exist → gate=ALLOW/first, no collision, no takeover token needed. **No shard-3 artifact was written and no INDEX.jsonl line was appended for this shard** — this sub-entry documents a blocking discovery instead, per GROUNDED_NOT_SUMMARY / anti-cheat spirit (do not write false-labeled evidence to the shared ledger).
- **<门控> (surface check only, insufficient)**: `server_health` on mac IDA confirmed `status=ok`, `uptime_sec=5744–5848` across calls, `<反编译器>_ready=true`, `idb_path` containing `AiMaMi 1.1.8 universal.app` (not 1.0.9/1.1.1) — this is exactly what red line 17 requires today, and it **passed**, yet the underlying evidence was still wrong. Red line 17 checks module name only, not instruction-set/architecture-slice, so it cannot catch this class of defect.
- **critical finding**: the 1.1.8 binary at `raw/binary/AiMaMi 1.1.8 universal.app/Contents/MacOS/AiMaMi` is a genuine Mach-O **universal (fat) binary** containing two architecture slices — confirmed via `lipo -info` → `Architectures in the fat file: ... are: x86_64 arm64` and `file` → `[x86_64:Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64] [arm64]`. The single loaded IDB (`AiMaMi.i64`, one `list_instances` entry, no second instance available) is analyzing the **x86_64 slice**, not arm64 — confirmed directly via `disasm` on `get_relay_proxy_status` (`0x1004c6320`): raw mnemonics are `push rbp` / `mov rbp, rsp` / `push r14` / `push rbx` / `sub rsp, 50h`, i.e. native x86-64 machine code, not ARM64 (`stp`/`ldp`/`x0`-style). By contrast, the 1.0.9 macOS baseline on disk (e.g. `raw/aimami/1.0.9/macos/system/get_system_info/ida/pseudocode/0001_get_system_info_owner_cmd_6dde4e8d.c`) is genuinely ARM64 (`__usercall ... @<X0>`, register comments `x0`/`x19`/`x20`/`x24`). So **every "macos-arm64" 1.1.8 finding produced against this IDA session this round — the thread-model survey, `owner-map-118.jsonl` (angle A), and mac-shard-1 (already committed to `INDEX.jsonl`/this file) — was actually decompiled from the x86_64 slice while being labeled/pathed as `macos-arm64`.**
- **concrete false-positive this already produced (caught before write)**: while diffing `graceful_restart_for_update` for shard-3, the 1.1.8 (x86_64) decompile builds a 6-byte literal that decodes to `"x86_64"` (dword `0x5F335F5F`→`"x86_"`... exact bytes `x86_` + `64`) at the exact stack slot where the 1.0.9 (arm64) baseline for the sibling `get_system_info` builds a 7-byte literal `"aarch64"`. Read naively this looks like a genuine 1.0.9→1.1.8 app-level delta (hardcoded arch string changed); it is actually a **decompilation-environment artifact** — the 1.1.8 side reports its own architecture as `"x86_64"` simply because IDA is disassembling the x86_64 slice of the fat binary, not because the app's real arm64 behavior changed. This is the exact shape of false-positive the four-angle-completeness / anti-cheat rules exist to catch; it was not written to any shared artifact.
- **root cause (best guess, unconfirmed)**: `raw/binary/AiMaMi 1.1.8 universal.app/Contents/MacOS/AiMaMi.i64` is the only `.i64` present for 1.1.8 macOS (no separate arm64-only IDB exists anywhere under `raw/binary/`); whoever first opened this universal Mach-O in IDA appears to have accepted the x86_64 slice (either by dialog default or `autonomous`-style auto-pick) instead of arm64, and every subsequent session in this round (including this one) inherited that single wrong IDB via `server_health`'s module-name-only check.
- **scope impact**: `mac-shard-3/8` was **not produced** (16 commands: `get_relay_proxy_status, get_system_info, get_usage_refresh_interval, graceful_restart_for_update, has_notch, hotspot_ready, import_accounts_from_file, import_relay_config, import_remote_device_secret_if_empty, import_skill, inject_voice_text, load_bootstrap_state, load_change_analytics, load_custom_instruction_state, load_installed_skills, load_mcp_servers` — raw x86_64-based decompiles for the 14 non-orphan commands were pulled into a local scratchpad only, not written to `intermediate/` or `INDEX.jsonl`). **`mac-shard-1` (already committed) and the `threadmodel`/`owner-map-118` sub-entries above should be treated as unverified against true arm64 until re-checked** — their control-flow/callee-level claims are likely still directionally correct (Rust codegen logic is largely architecture-independent), but any claim sensitive to raw architecture, register/stack layout, or `#[cfg(target_arch=...)]`-gated code paths is unconfirmed.
- **not attempted (needs explicit user/owner decision, out of this producer's authority)**: reloading the mac IDA session against the arm64 slice specifically (`open_file` with `new_database=True` on the same fat binary would launch a second IDA instance and may hit the same default-slice problem without a human present to choose arm64 in the dialog, or would need `autonomous=True` behavior confirmed to pick arm64) — this is an infrastructure-level fix with cross-machine blast radius (other concurrent producers may depend on the current instance) and touches already-committed canonical evidence (mac-shard-1), so it was left for explicit user direction rather than performed unilaterally.
- **round status**: `mac-shard-3/8` remains **open/blocked**; round `status` stays `in-progress`.
